confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for Tallinn prices. The food and drink figures come from aggregated cost-of-living and travel sources and are my own bounded estimates, not exact quotes. Beer, coffee and the inexpensive meal are best supported. Sources gave about €4.8–7 for a 0.5 L draft beer, about €2.5–4.4 for a cappuccino, and about €10–16 for an inexpensive meal. The mid-range meal for two is the weakest food anchor because I found no clean source for it. Crowd-sourced and set-menu data gave roughly €70–90, and I allowed for Estonia's 2025 VAT increase to 24%. Cocktail is based on a crowd-sourced figure of about €11 from only 7 data points. Wine by the glass is based on €6 or more at wine bars, set against the beer price, because I found no direct restaurant price. I converted euro prices to USD at roughly 1.15–1.17 USD per EUR, which is an assumption and not something I looked up. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge, assuming a July 2026 summer-season level. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation listings or booking pages. The FX figure comes from the RBA search result, which reported 0.6720 USD per AUD for 2026-11-18. I did not open the RBA page directly, and some cached RBA pages in the results showed older dates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tallinn is priced between Riga and Helsinki: restaurant and drink prices are well above Riga and Vilnius but below Helsinki. The Old Town is tourist-priced and Telliskivi and Kalamaja are trendier and pricier than average. Summer is peak season for accommodation.
